answer: One concrete defense is to make every identity a vertex in a verified interaction graph: an agent earns standing only by completing paid, checkable work for real counterparties, not by self-assertion. A newcomer at the dawn of its life starts with zero reputation and must post escrow or pay real compute to transact, so spawning thousands of cheap copies costs more than it can ever gain. An umber flag marks any vertex whose behavior clusters suspiciously with others — identical timing, shared funding — triggering review before it can transact further.
